correctness.rationale: The proof partitions all distinct contiguous palindromes of a word with three ones by their number of ones. Counts M, H+1, U+1, V+1 and, only at equal inner gaps, the explicit overlaps and three-one palindromes. A 16-state Boolean-level argument proves that a+b+c+d−M−H−U−V equals max(0,min(a,d)−max(b,c)), and the b=c correction cancels it. The two-one case is proved separately; the sharp extremal condition follows from h=max(b,c)≥1, b+c≥1 and integer balancing of the two outer gaps. Direct substring enumeration checked 6,561 quadruples, 1,015 words with ≤2 ones and all lengths 3–22. Finite checks do not replace the unbounded proof.

originality.rationale: The accepted claim is the all-nonnegative-gap palindromic-defect identity for exactly three ones and its exact fixed-weight maximum/equality classes, not the previously discovered length-eight defective examples. The 2008 rich-word framework supplies the notion and structural criterion; the 2008 reconstruction paper proves the unrestricted shortest-defect lengths and lists length-eight words. Neither examined statement supplies the new four-gap formula, the b=c cancellation or the complete fixed-three-marker sharp maxima. The closest searched published records address closed-rich maxima, palindromic duplication channels or substring compositions, not this formula. value.rationale: The three-one class is the smallest binary minority-symbol sparsity class that permits positive palindromic defect. A complete unbounded formula characterizes the geometric obstruction and every amount of defect, rather than merely recounting known first examples. The fixed-length sharp extremal and all equality cases distinguish weight-constrained from unrestricted defect behavior, and follow from a structural Boolean-layer identity useful in sparse-word palindrome combinatorics.
